Just how, Agamemnon, great field marshal . . . most grasping man alive, how can the generous Argives give you prizes now? I know of no troves of treasure, piled, lying idle, anywhere.

glosses: present participle and gerund of grasp
The act of one who grasps or covets.

examples.text: These are my connections, my attachments. Maybe all I really am is the sum of all these connections, these fearful longings and graspings.

glosses: The act of making an unreasonable profit not justified by the corresponding assumption of risk, or by doing so unethically or opportunistically.

examples.text: Pfizer has made nearly $26bn (£21bn) in revenues in the first three months of the year, the bulk from its Covid-19 vaccine and new pill to treat the virus, prompting fresh accusations of pandemic profiteering.

glosses: present participle and gerund of profiteer
